Definition — Upper bound, supremum, maximum
      
        For a nonempty $A\subseteq\mathbb R$, $u$ is an upper bound if $a\le u$ for all $a\in A$, and $A$ is bounded above if it has one. For such an $A$ the supremum $\sup A$ is the least upper bound: (i) $a\le\sup A$ for all $a\in A$, and (ii) for every $\varepsilon\gt0$ some $a\in A$ has $a\gt\sup A-\varepsilon$ (if $A$ is not bounded above, $\sup A=+\infty$, see the next box). If $\sup A\in A$ it is the maximum. Infimum (greatest lower bound) and minimum are symmetric, $\inf A=-\sup(-A)$, and $\sup_{x\in X}f(x):=\sup f(X)$. Completeness of $\mathbb R$: every nonempty set that is bounded above has a supremum in $\mathbb R$.
